# `add_list`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Create a named object list in the persistent object-list configuration.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xcd1f0, ObjListConfig::AddList @0x6c3600 (64-bit build) |

Creates a list whose display name is the supplied string. The stored key is derived from a timestamp and the name is stored as the key's value, so names need not be valid XML identifiers; any string, including an empty one, is accepted (a client SHOULD reject empty names itself). A duplicate display name (exact string compare) is rejected with 225. This is the object-list store, distinct from the legacy plan store and from the held ViewPlan.

Side effects: Creates a new list entry in the persistent XML configuration, synchronously. No event is emitted by the handler.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"add_list"`. [READ] |
| `params` | string\|array | no | - | The list display name, as a bare string or as a one-element array whose first element is used (extra elements ignored). Absent, null, empty array or a non-string gives 105. No length check; the empty string is accepted and stored as a list named "" (markup escaping on round trip INFERRED from the XML library). [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | params is absent, null, an empty array, or not a string (or one-element array holding a string) | `expected string param` |
| 225 | A list with the same display name already exists | `xml item already exists` |
| 234 | The device's object-list store has no file configured (a device-side fault; not caused by the list name) | `xml file name is empty` |
| 226 | Creating the XML key failed | `fail to create xml key` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

The helper sets 236 while enumerating an empty or failed store but continues creating the list, so 236 is not an unconditional reply and may be followed by success. The close result is ignored; persistence failures below the helper are not established as RPC errors.

## Example

Request, create:

```json
{"id":21,"method":"add_list","params":"Winter targets"}
```

Request, create-array-form - One-element array form (first element used):

```json
{"id":22,"method":"add_list","params":["Winter targets"]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"add_list","result":0,"code":0,"id":21}
```

Reply, duplicate:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"add_list","error":"xml item already exists","code":225,"id":23}
```
